known_information: Issue: ### Microsoft PowerToys version 0.79.0 ### Installation method PowerToys auto-update ### Running as admin No ### Area(s) with issue? Peek ### Steps to reproduce When using Peek, the window that opens is centred on the screen and of a specific size (which I believe is relative to the resolution and monitor size being used). However after resizing the window so it is more appropriate (rather than the default which is widescreen), the window size/position is not maintained after closing the window and using Peek again. ### ✔️ Expected Behavior I would expect the window position and size to be maintained/remembered after closing Peek and when re-using Peek. ### ❌ Actual Behavior The window position and size defaults back to a widescreen form which is not appropriate behaviour on Windows when the options to maintain size/position are selected in the Display settings (see attached snippet). ![image](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/assets/16537497/d5adc992-237b-43ff-8ba9-4d613134ef04) ### Other Software N/A

Comment by JeffreyMercado: This is particularly problematic for me since I also have an ultrawide with secondary that's half the width (5120x1440+2560x1440). My setup is used as if it was a 3-monitor setup and use right half of the widescreen as my "primary." Since it opens at a fixed size and position relative to the monitor, it peeks the most important part of source files outside of my typical view (text appears on the "left" screen side relative to what I'm usually looking at). This would be a very handy tool for me but as it stands with this "bug," it's completely useless to me. If it could at least work similarly to the default windows behavior and remember size and _exact_ position (default is slightly offset from the last use), that would be great.
